The issue was that a return annotation of `"None"` (as a string) was being evaluated as `NoneType` instead of `None`, which caused inconsistencies in how FastAPI handles bodiless responses (e.g., for returning a `204 No Content` status code).

I modified `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` in the `get_typed_return_annotation` function to explicitly check if the annotation is the string `"None"` and return `None` in that case. This ensures that forward references to `None` are treated the same as the `None` type itself for return annotations, while leaving parameter annotations unaffected.

The fix was verified using a reproduction script that confirmed `-> "None"` now correctly returns `None`.
